overall: The AG found a violation only for members' failure to file OML certification forms within two weeks of appointment, ordered compliance and certification for the outstanding members, and declined or found untimely the other ten allegations.

allegations.summary: Commission members failed to complete the required Open Meeting Law certification form within two weeks of appointment; the Commission did not dispute this.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when its members failed to complete the required certification form within two weeks of appointment to the Commission.

allegations.summary: The Commission held fewer meetings in a year than legally required.
allegations.key_passage: The above matters, even if true, would not violate the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, and we therefore decline to review them.

allegations.summary: The Chair consulted with the City rather than other Commission members when deciding to cancel the February meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The above matters, even if true, would not violate the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, and we therefore decline to review them.

allegations.summary: The Chair refused to explain an OML complaint discussed at a meeting and made inappropriate comments about the person who asked.
allegations.key_passage: although an allegation of unprofessional conduct or incivility does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, our office encourages civility during meetings of public bodies.

allegations.summary: The Chair left off meeting notice topics that fellow Commission members had requested.
allegations.key_passage: The law does not require the chair to add topics to a notice that are requested by fellow members of the public body.

allegations.summary: The Chair consulted with the City rather than other Commission members when changing the day of the monthly meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The above matters, even if true, would not violate the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, and we therefore decline to review them.

allegations.summary: The Commission held an election for only one position.
allegations.key_passage: The above matters, even if true, would not violate the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, and we therefore decline to review them.

allegations.summary: The Commission's website lacks contact information for the Commission.
allegations.key_passage: The above matters, even if true, would not violate the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, and we therefore decline to review them.

allegations.summary: A member of the public was not allowed to record the January 11 open session meeting; complaint filed 48 days later.
allegations.key_passage: The Commission’s January 11 meeting was conducted entirely in open session; therefore, any violation that occurred during the meeting was discoverable at the time it occurred.

allegations.summary: Meeting notice topics such as 'conversations with board members' and 'email etiquette' were alleged to be insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, there are no meeting notices for which a complaint about the specificity of the notice would be considered timely, and we therefore decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Commission meeting minutes were alleged to be inaccurate, missing details of votes and topics discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Based on a cursory review of the Commission’s meeting minutes posted online, we find no set of minutes for which the February 28 complaint would have been timely filed.

remedy: Commission members who have not yet done so must complete the Open Meeting Law certification form within 30 days of the letter date.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
